question_text: Module 7 traces how God has related with humanity in stages — first through the prophets, then through the Son made flesh, and now in a new way. In this present "age of the Spirit," how does God chiefly relate with and lead the believer day by day?
answer_options: Through the indwelling Holy Spirit, who lives in us and leads us into all truth.
Through angels and prophets only, exactly as before Christ came.
Through the written law alone, apart from any personal relationship.
Through occasional visits of the Spirit that happen only during church services.
correct_answer: Through the indwelling Holy Spirit, who lives in us and leads us into all truth.

question_text: Scripture commands, "grieve not the holy Spirit of God" (Ephesians 4:30). The module builds an important argument on this command. What does the fact that the Holy Spirit can be grieved prove about Him?
answer_options: That He is an impersonal force or energy we can switch on and off.
That He is a Person — only a person can be grieved, so He has mind, will, and emotion.
That He is somehow less than fully God.
That He relates only to mature, long-time believers.
correct_answer: That He is a Person — only a person can be grieved, so He has mind, will, and emotion.

question_text: The module pictures the Holy Spirit as a "new roommate" who makes His home in the believer. According to 1 Corinthians 6:19, when does He take up permanent residence, and what does the believer become?
answer_options: Only after years of obedience; the believer becomes a prophet.
Only when a believer speaks in tongues; the believer becomes an apostle.
At the new birth; the believer's body becomes a living temple of the Holy Spirit.
At water baptism only; the believer simply becomes a church member.
correct_answer: At the new birth; the believer's body becomes a living temple of the Holy Spirit.

question_text: Paul says believers are "sealed" and given "the earnest of the Spirit" (2 Corinthians 1:22; Ephesians 1:13-14). The module explains these two word-pictures. What do the seal and the earnest signify together?
answer_options: A seal marks God's ownership of us; an earnest is a deposit guaranteeing our full eternal inheritance.
A seal hides our sin from God; an earnest is a reward we earn by good works.
Both simply mean we must keep working hard to hold on to our salvation.
A seal is water baptism; an earnest is faithful church membership.
correct_answer: A seal marks God's ownership of us; an earnest is a deposit guaranteeing our full eternal inheritance.

question_text: The module gives a clear pathway for receiving the Holy Spirit (Luke 11:13; Galatians 3:2; 4:6). Which statement best captures its central principle?
answer_options: He is earned by long fasting and striving until we finally feel worthy of Him.
He is received by faith as the Father's gift to His children — not earned by striving or works.
He is given only to church leaders who hold a ministry office.
He is obtained by carefully keeping the works of the law.
correct_answer: He is received by faith as the Father's gift to His children — not earned by striving or works.

question_text: The module groups the nine manifestation gifts of 1 Corinthians 12:8-10 into three families, according to what each family does. What are the three categories?
answer_options: Gifts of Service, Gifts of Giving, and Gifts of Mercy.
Gifts of Teaching, Gifts of Leading, and Gifts of Helps.
Gifts of Revelation (they reveal), Gifts of Power (they do), and Gifts of Inspiration (they speak).
Gifts of Tongues, Gifts of Healing, and Gifts of Faith.
correct_answer: Gifts of Revelation (they reveal), Gifts of Power (they do), and Gifts of Inspiration (they speak).

question_text: The module distinguishes the nine manifestation gifts from the five-fold ministry offices (Ephesians 4:11). Which contrast does it actually teach?
answer_options: Both the gifts and the offices are given only to a select few leaders.
The offices are momentary manifestations; the gifts are permanent lifelong callings.
The nine gifts can operate through ALL believers as the Spirit wills, while the five-fold offices are callings given to SOME.
The gifts replaced the offices entirely in the New Testament church.
correct_answer: The nine gifts can operate through ALL believers as the Spirit wills, while the five-fold offices are callings given to SOME.

question_text: Galatians 5:22-23 says "the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace...". The module stresses that Paul writes "fruit," not "fruits." Why does this single word matter?
answer_options: The Spirit's work is unified — it is ONE fruit with nine expressions that grow together, so maturity means balanced growth in all of them.
We may pick the one or two expressions we like and simply ignore the rest.
Each expression is a separate fruit earned by a separate act of willpower.
Only love truly matters; the other eight are optional extras.
correct_answer: The Spirit's work is unified — it is ONE fruit with nine expressions that grow together, so maturity means balanced growth in all of them.

question_text: The module corrects a common misconception about how the fruit of the Spirit is produced. Which statement reflects the truth it teaches?
answer_options: I must work hard to manufacture the fruit by my own willpower.
Bearing fruit is mainly about polishing my external behaviour.
The Spirit produces the fruit as I abide in Him; it is nature transformation and evidence I already have God's favour.
Bearing fruit is the way I earn God's favour in the first place.
correct_answer: The Spirit produces the fruit as I abide in Him; it is nature transformation and evidence I already have God's favour.

question_text: The keystone verse of the module is Acts 1:8: "But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you...". According to the module, what is this power primarily given for?
answer_options: For personal comfort and private blessing only.
For empowered witness and a victorious life — boldness, holiness, discernment, and carrying the gospel to the ends of the earth.
For gaining status and an impressive ministry title.
For speaking in tongues and nothing else.
correct_answer: For empowered witness and a victorious life — boldness, holiness, discernment, and carrying the gospel to the ends of the earth.
